record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What is the length of the longest word avoiding strongly k-abelian nth powers?

evidence.quote: What is the length of the longest word avoiding strongly k-abelian nth powers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. For a positive integer $k$, two words $u,v \in \Sigma^*$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u \sim_k v$, if $|u|=|v|$ and for every word $w$ with $|w|\le k$, the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $v$. 

For an integer $n\ge 2$, a word $W \in \Sigma^*$ is called a strongly $k$-abelian $n$th power if it can be written as $W = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$, where $w_1,\dots,w_n$ are words of equal length such that $w_i \sim_k w_j$ for all $i,j \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, and additionally every length-$|w_1|$ factor of $W$ that begins at a position $1, |w_1|+1, 2|w_1|+1, \dots$ within $W$ shares this $k$-abelian equivalence (i.e. the $n$th-power structure is enforced not only blockwise but consistently across overlaps).

A word $u$ is said to avoid strongly $k$-abelian $n$th powers if no factor of $u$ is a strongly $k$-abelian $n$th power.

Problem: Given integers $k\ge 1$, $n\ge 2$, and an alphabet $\Sigma$ of size $q\ge 2$, determine the length of the longest finite word over $\Sigma$ that avoids strongly $k$-abelian $n$th powers (or show that arbitrarily long such words, or infinite such words, exist).
artifact.status_search_result: A 2013 work "Strongly k-Abelian Repetitions" addresses avoidability of strongly k-abelian n-th powers, indicating that such powers are unavoidable in certain regimes, which would make the longest avoiding word finite. However, the exact length as a function of k, n, and alphabet size does not appear to have a known closed-form solution in the literature surveyed, so the precise quantitative question appears to remain open or only partially answered.

status_evidence.title: Strongly k-Abelian Repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies avoidance of strongly k-abelian n-th powers; results indicate unavoidability in various settings.
status_evidence.claim: Strongly k-abelian n-th powers have been shown unavoidable in certain parameter regimes, but exact extremal lengths are not given in standard form.

status_evidence.title: On the k-Abelian Equivalence Relation
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of k-abelian equivalence and related repetition avoidance problems.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative bounds on longest words avoiding strongly k-abelian powers are not given as a closed solution.
